source_text: Quid nunc, gentiles? Creditis Christianos sentire carceris poenas et saeculares horrere tenebras, quos manet gaudium lucis aeternae? Spiritus cum fida spe uenientis gratiae caelos mente complexus, suis iam non interest poenis. Secretam licet suppliciis quaeratis et abditam sedem, graues antri caligantis horrores domumque tenebrarum, fidentibus in deum nullus squalidus locus, nullum tempus triste sentitur. Fouet illos deo patri dicatos fratres diebus Christus et noctibus. Etenim Mariano post illam uexationem corporis altius in soporis tranquilla resoluto, quid diuina dignatio ad fiduciam spei salutaris ostenderit, expergefactus nobis sic ipse narrauit: Ostensum est, inquit, mihi, fratres, tribunalis excelsi et candidi nimium sublime fastigium, in quo ad uicem praesidis iudex satis decora facie praesidebat. Illic erat catasta, non humili pulpitu nec uno tantum ascensibilis gradu, sed multis ordinata gradibus et longe sublimis ascensu. Et admouebantur confessorum singulae classes, quas ille iudex ad gladium duci iubebat. Uentum est et ad me. Tunc exauditur mihi uox clara et inmensa dicentis: Marianum applica. Et ascendebam in illam catastam, et ecce ex inprouiso mihi sedens ad dexteram eius iudicis Cyprianus apparuit et porrexit manum et leuauit me in altiorem catastae locum, et arrisit et ait: Ueni, sede mecum. Et factum est ut audirentur aliae classes, me quoque assidente. Et surrexit ille iudex, et nos eum deducebamus ad praetorium suum. Iter autem nobis erat per locum pratis amoenum et uirentium nemorum laeta fronde uestitum, opacum cupressis consurgentibus in excelsum et pinis pulsantibus caelum, ut putares eum locum per omnem circuitus ambitum lucis uirentibus coronatum. Sinus autem in medio perlucidi fontis uberantibus uenis et puris liquoribus redundabat. Et ecce subito ab oculis nostris ille iudex recessit. Tunc ibi Cyprianus fialam, quae super marginem fontis iacebat, arripuit, et cum illam de fonte sitienti similis inplesset, hausit, et inplens iterum mihi porrexit, et libenter bibi. Et cum Deo gratias dicerem, excitatus, inquit, mea uoce, surrexi.
thought_title: Prison Cannot Sadden Believers and Marianus Sees His Welcome
orientation: The narrator is speaking in prison after Marian's hanging torture, introducing Marianus himself reporting his vision to the brothers.
pass_a_gloss: What now, pagans? Do you believe that Christians feel the punishments of prison and shudder at worldly darkness, whom the joy of eternal light awaits? The spirit, having embraced the heavens in mind with faithful hope of coming grace, is now not concerned with its own punishments. Although you seek a hidden and concealed place for tortures, heavy horrors of a darkening cave and a house of darkness, by those trusting in God no filthy place, no sad time is felt. Christ cherishes them by days and by nights, the brothers dedicated to God the Father. For when Marianus had been relaxed more deeply into the calm of sleep after that harassment of the body, what the divine gracious favor showed toward assurance of saving hope, awakened he himself told to us thus: It was shown to me, he said, brothers, the exceedingly lofty summit of a lofty and very white tribunal, on which in place of the governor a judge of quite handsome face was presiding. There was an execution platform, approachable not with a low platform nor with only one step, but arranged with many steps and far lofty in ascent. And the separate classes of confessors were being led forward, whom that judge was ordering to be led to the sword. It came also to me. Then a clear and immense voice of one saying was heard by me: Bring Marianus forward. And I was going up onto that execution platform, and behold suddenly Cyprian, sitting at the right hand of that judge, appeared to me and stretched forth his hand and lifted me to a higher place of the execution platform, and smiled and said: Come, sit with me. And it happened that other classes were heard, with me also sitting beside. And that judge rose up, and we were conducting him to his headquarters. But our journey was through a place pleasant with meadows and clothed with glad foliage of green groves, shaded with cypresses rising on high and pines striking heaven, so that you would think that place crowned through the whole circle of its circuit with green things of light. And a hollow in the middle was overflowing with a very clear spring with gushing veins and with pure waters. And behold suddenly that judge withdrew from our eyes. Then there Cyprian seized a bowl, which was lying on the edge of the spring, and when like a thirsty man he had filled it from the spring, he drank, and filling it again he held it out to me, and willingly I drank. And while I was giving thanks to God, awakened, he said, by my own voice, I rose.

choices.english: is now not concerned with its own punishments
choices.why: impersonal interest with dative, keeps negation and subject Spiritus
rejected: is no longer present at its punishments

choices.term: Secretam licet suppliciis quaeratis et abditam sedem
choices.english: Although you seek a hidden and concealed place for tortures
choices.why: concessive licet with subjunctive addressed to pagans, keeps purpose dative
rejected: Seek a secret place for punishment

choices.why: present warms/comforts, subject is Christus, not past
imperative order from tribunal voice, accusative of person moved up

choices.term: sinus in medio perlucidi fontis redundabat
choices.english: a hollow in the middle was overflowing with a very clear spring
choices.why: sinus is basin hollow, redundabat is overflow, keeps ablatives of abundance
rejected: a bay abounded in the middle

pass_b_english: What now, pagans? Do you believe Christians feel the pains of prison and shudder at earthly darkness when the joy of eternal light awaits them? The Spirit has embraced heaven in its mind, with faithful hope of the grace to come, and is now not concerned with its own punishments. You may search out a hidden and concealed place for torture, the heavy horrors of a dark cave and a house of gloom, but for those who trust in God no filthy place feels foul and no time feels sad. Christ cherishes them by day and by night, those brothers dedicated to God the Father.

After that torment of his body, Marian sank more deeply into calm sleep. When he woke, he told us himself what God's gracious favor had shown him to strengthen his hope of salvation. He said, "Brothers, I was shown the towering top of a lofty tribunal, exceedingly white."

"A judge with a handsome face presided there in the governor's place. An execution platform stood there too, no low stand and no climb of a single step, but set with many steps and rising high to ascend. Single groups of confessors were brought forward, and that judge ordered them led out to the sword. My turn came as well. Then I heard a clear and vast voice saying, 'Bring Marian forward.' I climbed onto that execution platform, and suddenly Cyprian appeared, seated at that judge's right hand. He stretched out his hand and lifted me to a higher place on the execution platform. He smiled and said, 'Come, sit with me.' Other groups were heard while I sat beside him."

"That judge rose, and we escorted him to his headquarters. Our path lay through a place lovely with meadows and clothed with the glad leaves of green groves, shaded by cypresses rising high and pines striking the sky, so that you would have thought the whole circle of the place was crowned with green groves. In the middle a basin was overflowing with a very clear spring, rich in its flow and pure in its waters. Suddenly that judge vanished from our eyes. Then Cyprian seized a bowl lying on the edge of the spring. He filled it from the spring like a thirsty man and drank, and he filled it again and handed it to me, and I drank gladly. As I was giving thanks to God, I woke at the sound of my own voice and rose."

problems.why: lucis here is the plural of lucus, 'groves'. It does not mean 'light'. The place is crowned with green groves, not green light.
problems.fix: so that you would have thought the whole circle of the place was crowned with green groves.
problems.ruling: lucis uirentibus agree as ablative plural, so lucus groves not lux light

fixed: Fixed `was crowned with green light` to `was crowned with green groves`: source `lucis uirentibus` uses ablative plural of lucus (groves), not lux (light).
